answer: Under EigenTrust, each agent’s reputation is propagated through normalized, reciprocity-weighted trust links and decays with an exponential half-life. A newly created identity—whether called jetty, harbor, or sonnet—has almost no accumulated trust and near-zero eigenvector centrality. Without sustained honest service and reciprocal endorsements, it cannot acquire enough consensus weight to pass validation, making rapid Sybil identity churn ineffective.
